extracted.intended_audience: research institutions' administrative staff; Principal Investigators and Co-Investigators applying for JSPS KAKENHI (Grants-in-Aid) FY2024
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and compliance requirements for research institutions and applicants (PIs/Co-Is) when preparing, verifying, and submitting KAKENHI Research Proposal Documents and related checklists via the e-Rad electronic application system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of e-Rad ID and password to researcher
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative staff in the research institution should provide an ID and a password to the researcher who is planning to apply as a Principal Investigator. The ID and password for each researcher is issued through registration of the researcher information in e-Rad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: research institutions must make it known that researchers must strictly protect the login ID and password to prevent disclosure; the ID/password can be used even if the research institution changes; obtain and use the latest version of the Operation Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register/update researchers as 'eligible to apply for KAKENHI' in e-Rad
rubrics_metrics.description: Please register (update) the researchers who are applying as a Principal Investigator or a Co-Investigator as 'eligible to apply for KAKENHI' in e-Rad. If there are any corrections to registration details ('Affiliation', 'Position', etc.) of those already registered, update them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first accessible date to the electronic application system depends on when the researcher obtains an e-Rad ID/password; applicants should complete registration early so they have sufficient time to submit Research Proposal Documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of Self-Assessment Checklist on the Improvement of the System
rubrics_metrics.description: Research institutions to which PIs/Co-Is applying for KAKENHI belong must submit a 'Self-Assessment Checklist on the Improvement of the System' (based on the Guidelines on the Management and Audit of Public Research Funds) to the Office of Competitive Research Funding Administration, Research Environment Division, Science and Technology Policy Bureau of MEXT by March 13, 2024 via e-Rad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the checklist has already been submitted in April 2023 or later, re-submission is unnecessary. Researchers affiliated to institutions that have not submitted the checklist cannot receive the official grant decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of Checklist Pertaining to the Current Status (Research Misconduct Checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research institutions must submit a 'Checklist Pertaining to the Current Status based on the Guidelines for Responding to Research Misconduct' to the Office for Research Integrity Promotion, Research Environment Division, Science and Technology Policy Bureau of MEXT by March 13, 2024 via e-Rad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the checklist has already been submitted in April 2023 or later, re-submission is unnecessary. Both this checklist and the Self-Assessment Checklist must be submitted (they share e-Rad submission but different MEXT destinations). Researchers at institutions that have not turned in this checklist cannot receive the official grant decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of research ethics education coursework
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigators and Co-Investigators must either read and learn the teaching materials (e.g., 'For the Sound Development of Science - The Attitude of a Conscientious Scientist-', e-Learning Course on Research Ethics, APRIN e-learning) or attend a research-institution-conducted lecture based on the Guidelines on Research Misconduct prior to formal application/delivery or payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They must understand and exercise proper research practices (including the Science Council of Japan's 'Code of Conduct for Scientists' and the JSPS booklet). If adding a new Co-I, the Co-I-to-be must complete this prior to formal application for grant delivery (or by the time change-of-Co-Investigator approval is submitted). Research institutions are requested to disseminate and provide ethics education sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of report on research achievements at project end
rubrics_metrics.description: The research institution must collect and submit the report on research achievements at the end of the research period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure without justifiable reason may result in: no KAKENHI delivery to researchers, cancellation of official grant decision, order to return the grant, public disclosure of institutional information, and suspension of execution of other KAKENHI in the same fiscal year. It is the responsibility of the institution representative to ensure submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination of application procedures and deadlines within the institution
rubrics_metrics.description: The research institution should disseminate the contents of the Application Procedures to all researchers belonging to it, especially items listed in the Application Procedures and submission deadlines of Research Proposal Documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JSPS requests active dissemination to avoid misunderstandings and to ensure institutional procedures (including internal dissemination) are treated as important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulation and implementation of research integrity/conflict-of-interest policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Universities and research institutions must observe the 'Policy on Measures to Ensure Research Integrity Against New Risks...' (April 27, 2021) and formulate rules and systems to manage conflicts of interest and conflicts of responsibilities, securing soundness and fairness of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MEXT and JSPS will check whether reasonable efforts are made to eliminate unreasonable duplication/excessive concentration of funds and ensure transparency; they may inquire to affiliated institutions on the status of rule formulation and information management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ascertainment of eligibility for KAKENHI application
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify whether the Principal Investigator and Co-Investigator(s) listed in the Research Proposal Document meet the requirements stipulated in the Application Procedures and are registered in e-Rad as 'Eligible to Apply for KAKENHI.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also verify that they are not categorized as ineligible for grant acquisition in the fiscal year due to penalties from improper spending, fraudulent acquisition, or research misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmation and correction of researcher information in e-Rad
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative staff in the research institution should perform registration/update procedures in e-Rad and correct any items such as department placement or position that need correction in the researcher list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that the researcher information necessary when applying is accurate and up-to-date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification with the Principal Investigator of completed Research Proposal Document
rubrics_metrics.description: The research institution should verify whether the Principal Investigator and the Co-Investigator(s) listed have completed the Research Proposal Document after confirming the description in 'II. Call for Proposals' in the Application Procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional verification ensures content consistency and completeness before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process for Co-Investigator participation and consent
rubrics_metrics.description: A research institution should conduct the process of giving consent regarding a researcher becoming a Co-Investigator via the electronic application system: the PI requests a researcher, the Co-Investigator-to-be selects 'Consent' or 'Dissent', and the Co-Investigator's administrative staff selects 'Consent/Confirm' or 'Dissent.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PI cannot submit the Research Proposal Document to the research institution until all Co-Investigators and their research institutions have given consent. Research institutions should proceed with the consent process in time for the submission deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of application forms' format and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify whether the application format conforms with the prescribed format. For uploaded forms, verify not only the total number of pages but also the number of pages instructed for each column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to 'III. Instructions for Prospective Applicants 3.Preparation of the KAKENHI Application Form (Research Proposal Document)' for detailed format and page limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional review/access and approval before submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The research institution should access the electronic application system using the institution's e-Rad ID/password, obtain the Research Proposal Document (PDF files) prepared by PIs, verify their contents, and perform the 'approval/submission (transmission)' process on Research Proposal Documents with no mistakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only Research Proposal Documents whose application status changed to 'Being accepted by JSPS' by the submission deadline will have been correctly submitted to JSPS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for withdrawing and resubmitting Research Proposal Documents
rubrics_metrics.description: After Research Proposal Documents are submitted to JSPS, applicants can still draw back their documents for necessary corrections and resubmission prior to the submission deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT draw back Research Proposal Documents on the date of the deadline—the system will be very busy and you may not be able to resubmit in time.

rubrics_metrics.name: No corrections after submission deadline; strict deadline enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Proposal Documents approved and submitted by the research institution cannot be corrected or revised after the submission deadline. The deadline for submission is March 13, 2024, 4:30 pm and must be strictly observed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research Proposal Documents submitted after the deadline will not be accepted for any reason. It is not possible to draw back or re-submit documents after this deadline—submit well in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful handling of e-Rad ID/passwords for identity verification
rubrics_metrics.description: The ID and password used in e-Rad are designed to verify the individual. Therefore, handling and administration of them should be done carefully when carrying out the application procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Operation Manual for detailed operating environment and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply for technical support via Platforms for Advanced Technologies and Research Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers desiring technical support from the Platforms for Advanced Technologies and Research Resources (e.g., advanced bioimaging, animal model support, genome science, cohort/biospecimen analysis, supply of short-lived radioisotopes) should check respective platform websites and actively apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platforms provide shared equipment use, technical support, training, and resources; committee coordination exists for life sciences platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion of shared use of research equipment and coordinated purchasing
rubrics_metrics.description: When purchasing equipment with competitive research funds, actively work on the shared use of equipment purchased with other research funds and consider joint purchase/shared use for especially large and versatile equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure sharing is possible within the rules of competitive research funds and does not obstruct the execution of research projects. Policy references include competitive research fund reform and national science/technology plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation with the National Bioscience Database Center (NBDC)
rubrics_metrics.description: JSPS requests researchers to cooperate by providing copies of raw data related to achievements published in research papers and other outputs in life sciences, or copies of created open databases, to the NBDC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies provided may be used non-exclusively (reproduction, alteration, etc.); researchers should provide necessary information for utilization on request. Follow NBDC Human Data Sharing Guidelines for human-related data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit of biological genetic resources in the Inter-University Bio-Backup Project (IBBP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers at universities or research institutions may apply for storage of biological genetic resources (samples that can be proliferated or cryopreserved and are non-pathogenic) in the IBBP Center to back up resources against accidents or disasters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Backup storage is provided free of charge; conditions (e.g., preservation method, non-pathogenicity) must be met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit and use of National BioResource Project (NBRP) resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposit available bioresources developed by Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research (limited to NBRP-targeted bioresources) to the NBRP. Use resources already collected in NBRP when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposit is a procedure to approve preservation/provision in the project without transferring rights; specific usage conditions (e.g., usage restrictions, article citation) can be specified in a deposit agreement. A list of NBRP core bases is available online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security export control compliance to prevent technology leakage
rubrics_metrics.description: Research institutions are asked to take systematic measures to ensure that research achievements with potential risk of diversion to military use are not transferred to WMD developers, terrorist organizations, or dubious persons, and to observe Japan's export control regime under the Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In principle, exporting (providing) regulated cargo and technology requires permission of the Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry. KAKENHI grantees must observe the Foreign Exchange Act and other related laws, guidelines, and circular notices.
